repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
wait until((#MR_ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == true)
fired = false
}
wait until((#MR_ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false)
(#MR_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(10 SEC)
(#MR_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate implements a periodic `if` guard instead of a blocking rising-edge wait. The IR requires the cycle body to execute immediately upon the contact sensor transitioning to `false` (rising edge), whereas the candidate only checks the condition at the start of every 1-second iteration, missing the event if it occurs between checks.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with the standard rising-edge state machine: a persistent `fired` flag, a wait for the condition to become false (rearm), a wait for the condition to become true (trigger), and the body execution. This ensures the actions fire exactly when the edge occurs, preserving the IR's timing semantics.
